newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: AMMB plans cash call for bank expansion.
newsitem.headline: AMMB plans cash call for bank expansion.

text.p: AMMB Holdings Bhd plans to make a cash call in the near future to help the expansion of its commercial banking arm, company officials said on Wednesday.
The cash call will be "quite large" but details are still being discussed, said AMMB deputy chairman Azlan Hashim.
Officials said the cash call for Arab-Malaysian Bank Bhd will also help the bank to raise its shareholders' funds to 500 million ringgit quickly to qualify it as a Tier-1 bank.
"There will be a cash call," Azlan said. "We are trying to be Tier-1."

Arab-Malaysian Bank currently has shareholders' funds of about 250 million ringgit while AMMB holds the bank's irredeemable convertible unsecured loan stocks worth another 250 million ringgit, Azlan said.
Azlan said Arab-Malaysian Bank will open eight more branches by the year's end to bring its total outlets to 22.
Malaysia has a two-tier banking system, with banks in the first tier allowed to operate in a more liberal environment, including operating foreign currency accounts for exporters.
Azlan said the bank is still talking to commercial banking parties in Indonesia for the possibility of opening a joint venture bank.
